Subject: Security ops: Aria compliance feature asks — triage needed

Team —

Aria (prospect) sent a fairly dense list of security/compliance requirements and wants us to confirm feasibility and an estimated timeline. Short summary of asks from Emily Sanford (cc procurement):

- Tenant-scoped audit logs with exportable timeline for every API call (per-customer, immutable, searchable)
- Data retention buckets: 6 / 12 / 36 month options plus a legal-hold ability
- BYOK: customer-managed KMS; must support key rotation and proof of key destruction (HSM-based or KMS import/wrap)
- SSO: SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning, with 90-day inactivity cleanup policy
- SOC2 evidence: request for specific artifacts and log extracts for their auditors

They asked if we can commit to a delivery window; procurement mentioned 6–8 weeks as their ideal for evaluation. We should not promise that yet.

Asking for a quick internal triage: who can own each workstream (audit/export, retention, BYOK/KMS integration, SSO/SCIM, SOC2 evidence package)? What are the major blockers (security signoff, platform infra changes, dedicated/private only constraints)? If we need to propose an alternative (e.g., Dedicated or Private deployment to meet BYOK/HSM requirement), please say so.

Can each owner reply with: 1) feasibility (yes/partial/no), 2) effort estimate (sprint-weeks), 3) blockers and required approvals? I'll consolidate and reply to Aria with an internal timeline and MAP.

Thanks —
Jonas
Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Quick clarifying question: is Aria evaluating Hosted API or did they indicate they will require Dedicated/Private from day one? BYOK with HSM is typically a gating requirement for Private; we can sometimes offer a managed-KMS path on Dedicated depending on the contract.

I can do the retention + audit log schema triage. Initial thoughts: audit exports are straightforward as a pipeline (logcollector -> S3 staging -> per-tenant export), but immutability and chain-of-custody proof will need legal/compliance signoff. Retention tiers are doable but will need a UI/API toggle and background job to enforce deletions/legal-hold bypass.

Feasibility: audit/export = partial (need compliance), retention policies = yes (engineering effort). Effort estimate: audit+export pipeline ~ 3 sprint-weeks (2 eng + 1 infra), retention UI/API ~ 2 sprint-weeks. Blockers: SOC/compliance signoff, infra for export retention SLA.

—Mina

Thanks Jonas — putting Product on this as a priority for Q4 triage.

Proposal: split into three parallel workstreams and owners: 
1) Audit logs + export / SOC2 evidence (owner: Mina)
2) Retention + legal-hold UI/API (owner: Laura B.)
3) BYOK/KMS + SSO (owner: Vivek)

High-level timelines (rough): 1) 3–5 weeks to have a MVP export and evidence package workflow; 2) 2–4 weeks for retention buckets + legal-hold; 3) BYOK is bigger: 6–10 weeks depending on whether we need to support importable keys vs dedicated-HSM key wrap flow. SSO/SCIM work can be done in parallel (2–3 weeks) unless we hit enterprise provisioning gaps.

Blockers to flag immediately:
- BYOK: hosted environment limitations — if Aria insists on HSM-backed key custody, we likely need Private or a Dedicated+HSM design (security/legal needs to sign off).
- Audit immutability: we need an append-only storage plan and steps for signed manifests for chain-of-custody (legal/compliance help required).
- Timeline commitment: product cannot promise 6 weeks across all three streams; we should offer a staged MAP: export & retention first, BYOK pathing as conditional.

I started a short RFC and a JIRA ticket to track scope: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRFC-Compliance-asks and JIRA-INF-4821. Please update the ticket with any detailed designs or infra blocking notes.

—Laura

Quick technical notes on BYOK / audit shape: 

- BYOK: two viable patterns: 1) customer supplies a key in their cloud KMS and we use key-wrapping via a per-tenant envelope key (lower infra lift), or 2) direct HSM-managed key material that never leaves customer boundary (Private deploy or on-prem). Pattern 1 can be supported in Dedicated with configuration, pattern 2 requires Private.
- Key rotation/proof: we can log key rotation events and store signed rotation manifests; for proof of destruction we need signed attestations from HSM/KMS + procurement/legal acceptance.
- Audit schema suggestion: timestamp, request_id, tenant_id, route, model_version, response_size, token_count, prompt_hash (not raw prompt), user_agent, auth_subject. Avoid storing raw prompts in logs unless explicitly requested and consented.
- Performance: enabling full per-request logging for all fields increases storage & request latency slightly; recommend sampling or opt-in per-tenant.

Feasibility: BYOK (pattern 1) = feasible for Dedicated (4–6 sprint-weeks to implement and test); BYOK (pattern 2) = requires Private sales + infra (8+ weeks). Audit schema + export endpoints = feasible (3 sprint-weeks).

Blockers: legal to confirm allowed logged fields; security review for envelope key design; infra to provision dedicated KMS config.

—Vivek
